text:
How do suicides lie sleeping, Lord?
A clot at the mouth, both temples emptied,
the moons of their eyes pale and enlarged,
hands turned toward an invisible anchor?

Or do You come after the people have gone,
lower the lid over the blinded eye,
set the entrails right without pain or sound,
and cross their hands over the silent breast?

Does the rosebush the living water over their grave
paint its roses in the shape of wounds?
Is its scent sharp, its beauty dark,
its thinned branches woven with serpents?

Answer me, Lord: when the soul escapes
through the wet door of long wounds,
does it enter Your realm, cleaving the calm air,
or do maddened wings crackle?

Does a narrow, livid ring close around it?
Is the ether a field flowering with monsters?
In terror do they fail even to find Your name?
Or do they cry over Your sleeping heart?

Will no ray of sun reach them one day?
No water wash them of their red stigmata?
Is Your womb cold for them alone,
Your keen ear deaf, Your eyes shut tight?

So man claims, in error or malice;
but I, who have tasted You like wine, Lord,
while others call You Justice,
shall call You nothing but Love!

I know that man was always a hard claw,
the cataract a vertigo, the mountain roughness.
You are the vessel where all garden nectars
on Earth's orchards swell with sweetness!
